title: Hom(-,W) applied to a distinguished triangle: exactness at Y and at Z
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{d}X[1]$ a distinguished triangle and $W$ an object of $\mathcal T$. (i) If $a:Y\to W$ satisfies $a\circ u=0$, there is $b:Z\to W$ with $a=b\circ v$ (exactness of $\Hom(Z,W)\to\Hom(Y,W)\to\Hom(X,W)$). (ii) If $c:Z\to W$ satisfies $c\circ v=0$, there is $k:X[1]\to W$ with $c=k\circ d$ (exactness of $\Hom(X[1],W)\to\Hom(Z,W)\to\Hom(Y,W)$).

source.place: Lemma 0149 (lemma-representable-homological, line 386: Hom(-,W) is cohomological), (ii) applied to the rotated triangle (TR2)
